A_target.statement:
Let $h: A \to B$ be a [[Definition:Homomorphism (Abstract Algebra)|homomorphism]] of [[Definition:Algebraic Structure|algebras]] of any [[Definition:Signature|signature]].
Then:
:$A / \map \ker h \cong \Img h$
where $\map \ker h = \set {\tuple {a, a'}: \map h a = \map h {a'} }$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\theta$ be a [[Definition:Congruence Relation|congruence]] on an [[Definition:Algebraic Structure|algebra]] $A$.
Then $A / \theta$ is an algebra of the same [[Definition:Signature|signature]], with operations defined on representatives.

substitutions.the congruence on the algebra: the relation identifying elements with the same image under h
substitutions.the quotient algebra: the source collapsed by that relation
substitutions.the operations of the signature: the same operations, computed on representatives

derived.the induced map from the quotient to the: a bijective homomorphism, hence an isomorphism of algebras
derived.the group and ring cases: recovered by taking the signature to be that of groups or rings

object_map.reformulation: State the collapse in terms of a congruence rather than a distinguished kernel class, so that it applies to any signature.

validity_conditions: The relation identifying elements with equal image is a congruence, since homomorphisms commute with all operations of the signature.
The operations descend to classes because the relation is compatible with them, which is exactly the congruence condition.
For groups and rings the congruence is determined by a single class, the kernel, but for general algebras such as lattices no single class suffices and the congruence must be carried in full.
proof_plan:
$\theta$ is an [[Definition:Equivalence Relation|equivalence relation]].
For each $n$-ary operation $\omega$, if $a_i \mathrel \theta a_i'$ then:
:$\map h {\map \omega {a_1, \ldots, a_n} } = \map \omega {\map h {a_1}, \ldots, \map h {a_n} } = \map h {\map \omega {a_1', \ldots, a_n'} }$
Hence $\theta$ is a [[Definition:Congruence Relation|congruence]].
By the source result, $A / \theta$ is an algebra with induced operations.
